items.title: A GTA 6 Location Was Teased by Rockstar All the Way Back in 2021 — And What's Inside Was Worth the Wait
items.description: In 2021, Rockstar fans believed that a GTA 6 screenshot was snuck into the GTA trilogy collection, but there's more to this theory than meets the eye.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
SPOILER WARNING: This article features details on a GTA 6 Easter egg. Although it won't ruin the game's story or anything like that, we recognize some people want to organically discover and find interesting things on their own. You've been warned!

In 2021, Rockstar Games released the somewhat controversial remastered collection of the PS2 era GTA titles. It was... a mess, to say the least. However, one notable thing came from that collection, but fans weren't sure if it actually meant anything. There was a picture of a house in this new version of GTA: San Andreas that wasn't there in the original game, and it didn't look like a location from any other GTA game. Fans theorized this was actually our first look at GTA 6... and it turns out, they were right!

The house is real. It's located in Leonard County, in the suburb of Belville (shoutout Jared from the GTA mapping community for discovering this). However, that's just the tip of the iceberg. If you approach the house's garage, you can actually break in. Upon entry, it becomes clear this is a lair for some kind of conspiracy theorist. These aren't just ordinary in-universe ramblings — they're from someone who believes they are in a video game.

All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server.

The house is located in Belville. (https://t.co/hWt1Koz3uz) https://t.co/t2ZsSRPQFI

— GTA Wiki (@GTAWikiOfficial) November 18, 2026

Various notes and writings on the wall point out that they can't leave Lenoida at all. They tried to purchase a ticket to Los Santos and couldn't, nor could they drive out of the state, and instead are planning to get a boat to try and escape. They also noted that there are an extraordinary amount of doppelgangers in reference to NPCs, that there is nothing behind closed doors, their own neighbors can't enter their homes, and that people phase through walls or "glitch." There's also a graph that shows a comically large spike in violent crime and a bunch of 6s written all over the place, likely poking fun at some of the people who drove themselves mad theorizing about this very game.

Perhaps one of the most notable bits is that this conspiracy theorist has determined two people, who go by "J" (Jason) and "L" (Lucia), are immune to whatever problems they are experiencing, suggesting they have freedom and autonomy. Ironically, they may have the least amount of autonomy, though, since they are controlled by the player, but they respawn, are largely free of longterm legal consequences, and can cause tons of mayhem, so they're less restricted than NPCs.

It's a very silly Easter egg, and one that leans into the absurdity of the GTA community in many ways. It's unclear whether this house was always meant to be like this, or if someone at the studio decided to have some fun with it after they saw how mad it drove fans. Either way, it gave me a good chuckle.

In related news, GTA 6 is already shattering all kinds of records despite not being out globally. The game is driving tons of traffic to Twitch, YouTube, and Kick, with millions of people just watching the game. As for its critical reception, GTA 6 got a 10/10 from IGN and its critical praise has been echoed across the industry. In addition to being nominated for Game of the Year, GTA 6 is currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest rated game of all-time on Metacritic. While its position could change as more reviews trickle in over the next few weeks, it's clear this game is a gargantuan hit (though that likely isn't surprising).

items.title: Burger King’s Chocolate Whopper Prank Is Being Turned Into a Real Burger
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
In 2018, Burger King posted a Chocolate Whopper as an April Fool’s Joke. Nearly a decade later, the decadent burger is actually coming to life.

The Chocolate Whopper is coming to Burger King Korea’s new flagship restaurant, the Flameground, which recently launched its first location in Seoul. Flameground somehow turns Burger King food into a luxurious dining experience, showcasing the fast-food chain’s most experimental creations.

Burger King Korea accounts have shared AI-generated renderings of the Chocolate Whopper’s concept: layers of sauces and brownie patties encased in a chocolate fudge bun. We'll have to wait until the burger launches on November 19 to see what it actually looks and tastes like.

Unfortunately, the Chocolate Whopper is getting an extremely limited rollout. The burger isn’t even coming to general Burger King Korea locations, and is instead entirely restricted to the single Flameground restaurant, which requires a reservation.

The generated rendering is jam-packed, to say the least. Each burger is handmade, and orders are restricted to one per person with daily quantity limits. The Chocolate Whopper will also only be available as a dine-in experience, no take-out allowed, so Burger King is really trying to stop you from sharing.

Ahead of the launch, Burger King also reshared the original April Fool's prank video. The original prank featured some candied tomatoes the real version understandably skips out on.

Burger King Korea launched its first Flameground restaurant this past September. The Seongsu location currently offers three signature burgers: the K-Cube Galbi, the Philly Cheese Steak, and the Memphis BBQ. These are priced between ₩12,900 and ₩13,900, equivalent to around $10 USD. The restaurant has yet to announce pricing for the Chocolate Whopper.

The entire Burger King franchise has taken to wacky marketing, though most of the chain’s big promotions stick to licensed collaborations. For example, Burger King Italy just launched a Magic: The Gathering meal with an exclusive deck box everyone has been trying to get their hands on. Surprisingly, the fast-food chain has yet to announce any new food items inspired by GTA 6, which features the parody restaurant Burger Shot.

items.title: DevGamm Awards 2026 Winners Revealed
items.description: The 3rd annual DevGAMM Awards took place today, November 18, in Lisbon, Portugal, and celebrated 70 nominated games from 25 countries across 17 award categories. You can check out all of the winners right here, including Phonopolis, the game that led the way by securing both the Grand Prize and Excellence in Visual Art award.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
The 3rd annual DevGAMM Awards took place today, November 18, in Lisbon, Portugal, and celebrated 70 nominated games from 25 countries across 17 award categories. The show streamed on IGN and can check out all of the winners below, including Phonopolis, the game that led the way by securing both the Grand Prize and Excellence in Visual Art award.

The winners were decided by an international jury of 191 industry professionals from 40 countries. Beyond simply voting, however, the judges' "expertise and thoughtful feedback offered participating teams something that lasts considerably longer than an evening of applause."

Without further ado, here are the winners of The DevGAMM Awards 2026;

DevGAMM Awards 2026 Winners

Grand Prize

  • Dead As Disco by Brain Jar Games
  • Echoes of Mystralia by Borealys Games
  • Mortal Shell II by Cold Symmetry
  • MOUSE: P.I. For Hire by Fumi Games
  • Phonopolis by Amanita Design - WINNER

Excellence in Game Design

  • Desktop Explorer by Recurring Dream - WINNER
  • Froggy Hates Snow by Crying Brick
  • IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator by Nick Nieuwoudt, Dominik Latos
  • Rewindead by Spellwork AB
  • Timberborn by Mechanistry

Excellence in Visual Art

  • Micromega by COVEN
  • Midgardr by Holy Radish
  • MOUSE: P.I. For Hire by Fumi Games
  • Phonopolis by Amanita Design - WINNER
  • UNBEATABLE by D-CELL GAMES

Excellence in Narrative

  • Call of the Elder Gods by Out of the Blue Games
  • Desktop Explorer by Recurring Dream
  • Ledgerbound by OmniMegaSuperCorp - WINNER
  • Pieced Together by Glowfrog Games
  • Schrödinger's Call by Acrobatic Chirimenjako

Excellence in Audio

  • Band Wagon by Bippinbits
  • Dead As Disco by Brain Jar Games - WINNER
  • Phonopolis by Amanita Design
  • Ratatan by Ratata Arts Inc.
  • UNBEATABLE by D-CELL GAMES

Best Mobile Game

  • Gambonanza by Blukulele (Paul Giovannini) - WINNER
  • Pirates Outlaws 2: Heritage by Fabled Game Limited
  • Scritchy Scratchy by Lunch Money Games
  • Servant of the Lake by Rusty Lake
  • Twin Shot Deluxe by Nitrome Limited

Most Anticipated Game

  • Cards & Cannons by Flamehead Games UG
  • Crop by Carbonara Games - WINNER
  • Koshmar: The Last Reverie by Purple Ray Studio
  • PinKeep by Okomotive
  • Steel Soul Shaper by GENEPOP

Best Game in Early Development

  • BANDIT KNIGHT by Game Float
  • Bolt & Whalington by Orca Studio
  • Burdenfall by Leftovers Games
  • Code RAPID by Hitbreak Games LLC
  • Hold Your Dragons by Igor Krutov - WINNER

  • Dobbel Dungeon by Gamepie
  • MOLDRISE by Raffaele Picca - WINNER

  • Amnios by HES-SO (HEAD-Genève + HEdS)
  • As Long As You're Here by Autoscopia - WINNER
  • Fishbowl by imissmyfriends.studio
  • Grow Wild by SPECTRUM48

Best Game from Portugal

  • Hanno: A Magical Tale by One Way Eleven
  • NECROMENTAL by Digitality Games
  • Shelf Heroes by Fun Punch Games
  • War Doctor by Red Pine Studios - WINNER

DevGAMM Choice

  • Demon Bluff by UmiArt
  • HOMURA HIME by Crimson Dusk
  • inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories by Nagai Industries - WINNER
  • Monster Chef by Studio Pizza
  • Wax Heads by Patattie Games

Partner-Sponsored Awards

Epic Games Store Indie Spotlight

  • Dead As Disco by Brain Jar Games - WINNER
  • Fortune Seller by Kiwick Studios
  • Hank: Drowning On Dry Land by My Next Games
  • IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator by Nick Nieuwoudt, Dominik Latos
  • Luna Abyss by Kwalee Labs

Best Unreal Engine Game

  • Call of the Elder Gods by Out of the Blue Games
  • Dead As Disco by Brain Jar Games
  • Guns of Eschaton by Eschatology Entertainment
  • Mortal Shell II by Cold Symmetry - WINNER
  • The Occultist by DALOAR Studios

Best Indie Game by tinyBuild

  • Code RAPID by Hitbreak Games LLC
  • Hell Hold'em by Hell Hold'em
  • Meat Without Master by Neon Cocoa
  • Rewindead by Spellwork AB - WINNER
  • Tattered Banners by CookieByte Entertainment

Best Made With Unity Game

  • Dimraeth by Mudtek
  • Last Moon by Sköll Studio
  • Painted Kingdoms by Hectiq
  • Seaward by THE ROOF Interactive
  • Tempus Vitae by Whiteboard Games - WINNER

Best Godot Game

  • Band Wagon by Bippinbits
  • Burn With Me by Nozomu Games - WINNER
  • MOLDRISE by Raffaele Picca
  • My Card Is Better Than Your Card! by Utu Studios
  • Pathogenic by Aberrant Labs

For more, check out all you need to know about the DevGAMM Awards on their website.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

items.title: New Avengers: Doomsday Posters Reveal Key Characters and Tease Thor’s Odinforce
items.description: Marvel has revealed a massive lineup of new posters for Avengers: Doomsday, teasing major characters and a potentially huge upgrade for Thor.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Apparently, no one told Marvel that GTA VI is out today, because they've been busy showing off new glimpses of Avengers: Doomsday. In addition to a behind-the-scenes video featuring Robert Downey, Jr., Marvel has also revealed a massive lineup of posters showcasing the film's ensemble cast.

These 11 posters form one large montage showing the combined forces of the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Avengers in battle against Downey's Doctor Doom and his army of Sentinels and Doombots. Get a closer look at all these connecting posters in the slideshow gallery below:

These images tease some interesting new details for the film, like giving us a better look at Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler in costume and showcasing the Doombots (Doctor Doom's android servants/bodyguards) for the first time.

Perhaps most interesting is the poster featuring Chris Hemsworth's Thor and Chris Evans' Steve Rogers. Steve is wielding Mjolnir and channeling the weapon's signature blue lightning, but Thor's Stormbreaker is instead summoning yellow lightning. This has already led fans to speculate that Thor is now empowered by the Odinforce, signalling a major power upgrade for this already mighty Avenger. Though if the Doomsday trailers are any indication, that's not going to be enough to stop Doom.

We also have to wonder if the character pairings in these posters are significant and meant to tease various team-ups in the film. Certainly, Steve and Thor have a long history together. And we doubt it was merely coincidence that Marvel chose to pair Vanessa Kirby's Invisible Woman and Tenoch Huerta's Namor, given the (mostly one-sided) romantic attachment they share in the comics.

But what about the rest of the posters? Will Channing Tatum's Gambit partner up with Florence Pugh's Yelena Belova? What about Tom Hiddleston's Loki and Rebecca Romijn's Mystique? We'll have to wait until Doomsday hits theaters on December 18 to find out.

In the meantime, Marvel has already begun teasing Doomsday's sequel, 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, revealing that the film will be very different in terms of tone and genre. We've also learned that Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman have been given writing credits on Doomsday, suggesting that Deadpool and Wolverine will appear in the film.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

items.title: The Wachowskis Move to Reclaim The Matrix Rights From Skydance
items.description: The future of The Matrix franchise is suddenly in doubt, as Lilly and Lana Wachowski move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise from Warner Bros.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
The future of The Matrix franchise is looking increasingly murky. According to The Puck Report, Lana and Lilly Wachowski have formally notified Warner Bros. of their move to reclaim the copyright to the iconic sci-fi franchise.

If successful, the Wachowskis would regain the rights to the series on the 30th anniversary of the original film's release in 2029. This move comes as the studio is developing a fifth The Matrix movie, with Drew Goddard attached to write and direct and Lana Wachowski herself executive producing. That project may give the Wachowskis extra leverage in their negotiations with Warners.

Will this derail development on The Matrix 5? Not necessarily. The site also notes that WB's new parent company Skydance seems confident in its ability to negotiate a new deal, building on previous successes renegotiating the copyright for The Godfather and acquiring The Terminator rights in 2011. The Puck Report also alludes to a potential legal hurdle on the Wachowskis' side, as it could be argued that the original The Matrix screenplay was part of a work-for-hire arrangement with Warner Bros. back in the '90s.

All of this may suggest that the more likely outcome is that the Wachowskis negotiate a new, more lucrative deal and Skydance retains the rights to The Matrix for the foreseeable future. Despite Lilly Wachowski publicly distancing herself from the property, The Puck Report writes, "From what I hear, the sisters have been encouraging of the newest sequel and have even increased their involvement lately."

Little is currently known about The Matrix 5 beyond Goddard's involvement. There's currently no release date, nor is it clear whether series stars Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss will return or if the focus will shift to a new cast of cyberpunk martial artists. But the studio seems to have high hopes for the sequel, despite its predecessor, 2021's The Matrix Resurrections, proving to be a box office dud. It certainly didn't help that the film debuted during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on HBO Max the same day as it did in theaters, prompting a lawsuit from Village Roadshow.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

This move comes as the studio is developing a fifth The Matrix movie, with Drew Goddard attached to write and direct and Lana Wachowski herself executive producing. That project may give the Wachowskis extra leverage in their negotiations with Warners.

Will this derail development on The Matrix 5? Not necessarily. The site also notes that WB's new parent company Skydance seems confident in its ability to negotiate a new deal, building on previous successes renegotiating the copyright for The Godfather and acquiring The Terminator rights in 2011. The Puck Report also alludes to a potential legal hurdle on the Wachowskis' side, as it could be argued that the original The Matrix screenplay was part of a work-for-hire arrangement with Warner Bros. back in the '90s.

All of this may suggest that the more likely outcome is that the Wachowskis negotiate a new, more lucrative deal and Skydance retains the rights to The Matrix for the foreseeable future. Despite Lilly Wachowski publicly distancing herself from the property, The Puck Report writes, "From what I hear, the sisters have been encouraging of the newest sequel and have even increased their involvement lately."

Little is currently known about The Matrix 5 beyond Goddard's involvement. There's currently no release date, nor is it clear whether series stars Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss will return or if the focus will shift to a new cast of cyberpunk martial artists. But the studio seems to have high hopes for the sequel, despite its predecessor, 2021's The Matrix Resurrections, proving to be a box office dud. It certainly didn't help that the film debuted during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic and premiered on HBO Max the same day as it did in theaters, prompting a lawsuit from Village Roadshow.

items.title: GTA 6 Shatters Streaming Records Before It Even Launches Globally
items.description: GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 is already breaking records, despite not having even been out for a full day yet.

According to StreamCharts, GTA 6 shattered livestreaming viewership records following its release in New Zealand. Streamers began grinding the game at the earliest hours of the morning here in the United States thanks to handy loopholes on Xbox, allowing them to get a head start on things. As of 12:30 UTC today, the game crossed 6.38 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. This is nearly four times the previous record holder, which was Valorant's closed beta.

Twitch also provided first details about the game's performance using its own internal data to IGN.

  • GTA 6 smashed the Valorant on Twitch record, which stood at 1.7 million concurrent viewers in 2020.
  • On Twitch, GTA 6 is at tens of millions of hours watched, just a couple hours in.
    • The equivalent of more than 1,500 years of nonstop viewing.
  • Top GTA Streamer Rubius reached 311k live viewers for GTAVI within an hour of starting his broadcast.
  • GTA 6 in North America is technically not available to play yet but the streamer has already seen:
    • Twitch viewership is up 111% compared with this time last week.
    • At one point early this morning Twitch had more than 3.3 million live viewers in the GTA 6 category.

Twitch recently revealed to IGN that GTA 5 has accumulated 9 billion hours watched over the course of its entire lifetime, making it an absolute juggernaut for the platform. It's one of the most-watched games and it's likely that GTA 6 will retain get at least one or two more big boosts in viewership. The game is rumored to come to PC early next year and its online mode is also expected sometime in 2027, both of which will likely be events in their own rights.

IGN recently spoke with a number of content creators about how they're planning to handle GTA 6 and how long they think this game will remain relevant. Although some streamers believe this game will only be lucrative for a couple of weeks, others think there's potential for it to be mined for months and years to come.

IGN gave the game a 10/10, noting that the game is simply unmatched in its depth, quality, and detail. The game is currently the highest-rated game in history on Metacritic with an unprecedented 99 average score.

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played," reads an excerpt from our review.

For more GTA 6, check out our breakdown of how long the game can be depending on how you play, how it performs on Xbox Series S, and much, much more.

items.title: Robert Downey Jr. Teases Avengers: Doomsday With New Behind the Scenes Footage
items.description: Avengers: Doomsday star Robert Downey Jr. has discussed his role as Doctor Doom in a video that includes a few new behind the scenes clips from production.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Avengers: Doomsday star Robert Downey Jr. has discussed his role as Doctor Doom in a video that includes a few new behind the scenes clips from production.

While fans wait for a fresh, full-length Avengers: Doomsday trailer, Marvel released today's video to mark the fact that there's just one month left until Doomsday's December 18 release date.

There is nothing particularly revelatory about the brief snippets on show (and all the main footage from the film itself has been seen already), but fans will no doubt be poring over the scenes for further clues on what will unfold. And it's nice to hear a bit more from Downey Jr. on why he's back in the MCU once more, albeit as a very different character.

New mask. Same task. Robert Downey Jr. returns as Victor Von Doom.

In one month, Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere. Get tickets now: https://t.co/HReh5UfF1M https://t.co/tSxhzwRj8h

— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) November 18, 2026

"I kind of made my peace with it, and it felt so definitive by the time Endgame had been released," Downey Jr. begins, discussing his seemingly-permanent exit from the Marvel movie franchise in the last Avengers film. "When [the idea of returning] was first broached by Kevin, who said 'Hey, do you think you would ever...' And then, I really just thought 'How many surprises are left?'

"Any of these movies is only as good as its villain," Downey Jr. continued. "Victor is a master manipulator. And because of that, there's levels to the stakes here. It's such a long bench of talent. These people are people that I would do any movie with eight days a week. We just keep really trying to earn it with every breath. It's really hard to explain the love I have for this."

One shot in today's video shows Thor and Sam Wilson's Captain America meeting members of the New Avengers, with Shang-Chi and Ant-Man standing across from Yelena Belova and Bucky Barnes. It's a moment we've seen in a trailer already.

Another shot shows Steve Rogers, Cap, Shuri, Sue Storm, Red Guardian, Ghost, and John Walker standing in a forest. Is this Latveria?

There's not long to wait now until Avengers: Doomsday releases on December 18 and fans discover exactly what's in store.

Image credit: Marvel.

items.title: AI-Fueled Game Development Just Needs a Toy Story-Style Hit to Be Accepted, Former Take-Two CEO Says
items.description: Audiences will learn to love AI-generated games, the former CEO of GTA publisher Take-Two Interactive has said — as soon as they churn out a 'Toy Story moment' of quality.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Audiences will learn to love AI-generated games, the former CEO of GTA publisher Take-Two Interactive has said — as soon as they churn out a 'Toy Story moment' of quality.

Speaking to The Game Business, ex-Take-Two exec Ben Feder claimed that gamers who are sceptical about AI-made slop would be won over when a great example eventually comes along, with any resistance then melting away. Feder served at the company behind releases such as BioShock and Borderlands from 2007 to 2011, before subsequently joining Tencent Games, and serving on the boards of numerous other companies such as Bad Robot and Epic Games.

The comparison with Toy Story here is Feder equating the rise of generative AI (replacing games designed and coded by humans) to the emergence of computer animation in the world of animated movies (largely replacing hand-drawn techniques).

"When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.

"My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West," Feder continued. "In the East, they've already accepted it."

It's easy to see what Feder is implying, although the similarities between the two situations don't feel clear cut. Yes, Disney fans (and employees) were divided on the art of hand-drawn animation being superseded by an all-digital alternative. But the latter still requires considerable human skill to create — even if an artist is now using a stylus on an iPad rather than drawing with ink on paper.

Comparing this to the vibe-coded future of game development now rapidly bearing down upon us, generated by a few quick prompts and powered by GPU-hogging and potentially copyright-infringing AI tools, and it all seems something quite different.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Feder is now a managing partner at Tirta Ventures, a venture capital firm that is keen to invest in AI-generated games. "Our gaming backgroundhelps us identify AI-native platforms shaping how people play, create, and transact in digital environments," Tirta's website states.

The timing of Feder's statement — and his background at Take-Two — is also somewhat ironic, in the wake of Rockstar releasing the masterpiece that is GTA 6 after a decade of development, creating perhaps the biggest monument to game development without the widespread use of AI tools we're ever likely to see.

That's what the former boss of Take-Two thinks about AI, but what does the current boss of Take-Two think about the tech? Last month, Strauss Zelnick said AI is a valuable tool, but insisted humans will remain at the ehart of what the company does.

“One of our division heads has said to his team, ‘You’re not gonna be replaced by AI, but if you’re not careful you’ll be replaced by someone who knows how to use AI,’” Zelnick said. “I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward looking. [...]"

If you're keen to play the (human-created) GTA 6 this week, IGN has you covered — including the GTA 6 global release times, as well as details on the last-minute PS5 update you'll need to download. In case you missed it, last night we learned the real-life identity of GTA 6's Lucia. And we're now live with our GTA 6 launch blog, which we'll use to fill you in on everything else about the game over the coming hours.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's Lead Writer Has Left Sandfall to Help Game Devs Tell Better Stories
items.description: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead writer has left Sandfall to help other game developers think about story from the outset. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the narrative lead for Expedition 33, won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award earlier this year, and she’s since been consulting on stories across the industry.

Expedition 33 was her first video game (she came from a career in private equity), but it won more than 400 awards and received almost universal critical acclaim, in part due to its blend of real-time and traditional turn-based RPG mechanics, and partly because of its mysterious story, strong emotional beats, and brilliant characters.

Svedberg-Yen is now setting up a fund with the aim of advancing narrative design in video games and nurturing new writing talent.

“I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge,” Svedberg-Yen told GamesBeat. “We’re making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There’s so much disruption in the industry right now.”

Outside of the constant layoffs and upheaval in the industry, there’s also a sense, still, that narrative isn’t as respected as other parts of game design.

“A lot of studios think of narrative as a skin,” Svedberg-Yen said. “They think you can bring someone in later to make everything make sense.

“But when you start from the beginning, everyone is building from the same story and the different disciplines naturally reinforce each other.”

The award-winning writer believes this approach limits what games can achieve. Expedition 33 was designed with a narrative-first approach, with the game systems built around the story to reinforce the themes and pace the big moments out.

“Narrative was king,” she said. “It was always a narrative-first game. I think that’s why we were able to achieve the results that we did in terms of integrating all the different pieces into a wonderful collaborative whole. There was that consistency from the very beginning.”

According to Svedberg-Yen, she’s received messages from players about how Expedition 33 helped them deal with grief and navigate the world after suffering a personal loss.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t seem like we’ll see more of Svedberg-Yen’s work in video games any time soon. Outside of the fund, she has a couple of ideas for TV, but she left Sandfall in July “after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition.”

Following success at pretty much every major video game award show (most recently including scooping up Best Game at the BAFTA Awards), Sandfall Interactive is now busy planning its next project. Details of that currently remain under wraps, though the suggestion is that it will be another adventure set in the same Clair Obscur universe.

"Wearing its inspirations on its sleeve, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 paints itself into the pantheon of great RPGs with a brilliant combat system and a gripping, harrowing story," IGN wrote in our Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 review, dubbing it a "modern RPG classic."

items.title: You Can Now Order McDonald’s Through Discord
items.description: Discord has launched a McDonald's app, allowing users to order food through one of the most popular communication platforms.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Discord has launched a McDonald's app, allowing users to order food through one of the most popular communication platforms.

The integration, powered by Uber Eats, comes with its own lofi-inspired interface unique to Discord. The new app arrives just as gamers are starting to get their hands on GTA 6, the biggest game launch of all time, and it seems McDonald’s was worried players wouldn’t even be willing to look down at their phone screen.

The 'Order McDonald’s' feature is found in the Apps section of any Discord DM, channel, or server. You can choose to launch the app in a given server, which notifies everyone that you’re ordering McDonald’s, or access the app privately through its own DM.

Once inside, you get the option to Order Food or Play Game. Yes, there’s a game, but first, let’s talk about the food. Discord claims the purpose of the integration is to let you order food without tabbing out of a game or call. Yet, hitting the Order Food option actually takes you to an external Uber Eats link.

If you have the Uber Eats app, Discord on mobile takes you straight to your account, while the desktop version opens your default browser. In either case, you’ll need an Uber Eats account to actually order anything, and you’ll definitely still have to hit pause on whatever you're playing. At the very least, hitting the Order Food option gives you a neat little animation to approach the Drive-Thru window.

Now we can talk about the game. Fast Lane Feast is for when "you’re waiting for your order to arrive," but you can play the new minigame at any time. You drive along a little street, collecting burgers and fries for fuel, flying off ramps, and trying to avoid traffic. Controls are pretty minimal - using A and D to move left and right - but if you do get competitive, you can save your score to a global leaderboard.

McDonald’s isn’t the only fast-food chain testing trying to attract some loyal gamers. Wendy’s just launched an entire RPG, one of the very few game releases in the month of GTA 6. Wendy’s has also teased a collab with the Rockstar game, and McDonald’s might be the only company on the planet that hasn’t. For now, McDonald’s is offering the Pokémon Happy Meal, with a Home Alone collaboration planned for the holiday season.

items.title: Rockstar President Sam Houser Issues Rare Statement to Celebrate GTA 6 Launch
items.description: As GTA 6 launches around the world, Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement to celebrate the occasion and "many more years" of experiences ahead.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
As GTA 6 launches around the world, Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement to celebrate the occasion and "many more years" of experiences ahead.

While other high-ranking Rockstar staff have discussed GTA 6 in interviews thus far, the famously reclusive producer has now outlined his company's intentions with the game, and suggested there was much more to come in future.

"Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us," Houser began, in a statement shared with IGN's GTA 6 reviewer, Luke Reilly.

"This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special.

"Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities — and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes.

"We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you.

"Thank you, Sam Houser."

While Houser's rare statement is notable enough on its own, the mention of "many more years" of experiences from Rockstar will inevitably excite fans already wondering what's next from the company. While the base GTA 6 offers hundreds of hours of experiences to discover and enjoy, there is of course huge speculation surrounding the game's unannounced but inevitable online portion. As of yet, Rockstar has not discussed its next iteration of GTA Online at all, though fans expect to hear something of it sooner or later.

items.title: In GTA 6, Doomscrolling Is a Necessity If You Want to See Everything
items.description: Scrolling social media in GTA 6 is more than a distraction - it can help you see everything the world has to offer.
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
Ever since that first trailer, we knew social media would play an important part in GTA 6. A good chunk of those first 90 seconds was faux TikTok footage, after all. And now that reviews are out, and the game is live in New Zealand, Australia, and many other places on that side of the planet, we have a better idea of how GTA 6’s in-universe social media operates. One thing’s for certain: you’ll need to be scrolling if you want to see everything the world has to offer.

As part of IGN’s Ask Me Anything livestream earlier today, reviewer Luke Reilly explained how he unlocked a new mission chain based on a post he saw on Snapmatic, the GTA universe’s parody of Instagram.

“I was scrolling through the game’s social media, and I saw a post from this guy on a farm looking for a pilot, and it pings it on the map for you,” he said. “It’ll ping in an undiscovered part of the map that there’s something there because you’ve spotted it on social media.”

IGN’s Simon Cardy, who has also played over 100 hours of the game and is currently answering your questions over on our launch live blog, confirms that he also used social media to discover new opportunities, which are then automatically pinned to the game’s map.

Simon also notes that you’ll hear about opportunities on the in-game radio, although those are hints you’ll need to follow up on yourself – only certain mediums will pin a mission to your map. Aside from social media posts, pamphlets on local bulletin boards will also drop mission markers on your map, something Luke described in today’s AMA: “One of the cool things is that you see signs around [advertising] for a pilot. It’s visual storytelling; you can [follow the instructions] and go there and do jobs for this character that you meet.”

Bulletin boards are, of course, nothing new for video games – you’ll no doubt have picked up hundreds of bounties and side quests from boards in dozens of RPGs across the years. But GTA 6’s use of the internet and social media is more novel. Simon also notes that there are connections to be found across the in-game web, too – a story on the news app may lead you to investigate a topic on Snapmatic, which in turn will pin a new mission to the map.

In short: we may call it doomscrolling in real life, but it’s a pretty handy activity to do in GTA 6. While I expect there will be multiple ways to stumble across the game’s many, many missions, it seems a fun and authentic method to discover things on social media.

For more GTA 6, be sure to check out our breakdown of how long it takes to complete its campaign, as well as our brand new interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson. And if you want to see the game in action, you can watch 15 minutes of the game’s first mission.

items.title: MindsEye Dev Build a Rocket Boy Says Legal Action Against 'Several Third Parties' Will Help It Pay Off Its Mountain of Debt
items.description: After the disastrous release of MindsEye, its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
After the disastrous release of MindsEye, its collapsed developer, Build a Rocket Boy (BARB), is attempting to pay off its mountain of debt via legal action against “saboteurs” who it alleged contributed to the game's downfall.

Story-driven action adventure game MindsEye was initially designed to be a part of Everywhere, the ‘Roblox for adults’ creation platform led by former Grand Theft Auto design chief Leslie Benzies. BARB eventually switched to focus on MindsEye, with the company ballooning in size to over 500 staff at peak.

But MindsEye flopped hard when it came out in June 2025, with players calling it "broken," "buggy," and "the worst game of 2025." Soon after, BARB said it was “heartbroken” over the issues players had faced with the game, and promised to release a series of patches to fix the significant performance problems, glitches, and AI behavior bugs. Amid sweeping layoffs, Benzies told staff that the studio would bounce back and relaunch MindsEye, blaming its struggles on internal and external "saboteurs," among other things. CEO Mark Gerhard said the studio had been investigating what he called “criminal activity” that took place around the launch of the game.

However, in September this year it was reported that the Edinburgh-based company faced closure, with BARB slipping into administration. Today, on the eve of GTA 6's launch, an administrators’ proposal went live on BARB’s Companies House page — spotted by RedbullCola on ResetEra, (thanks Kotaku). The proposal details what BARB owes and to who, as well as how it plans to cover its debts.

The total debt comes to £61.7 million (approx. $81.2 million). The bulk of the debt belongs to NetEase (£36.4 million, approx. $47.9 million). NetEase is a major investor in BARB, having participated in multiple funding rounds including a $110 million Series D round in January 2024. According to company documents, BARB brought in more than £233 million (approx. $306 million) of investment by 2024. £19.90 (approx. $25... yes, $25!) is owed to ChatGPT company OpenAI.

Earlier this year, BARB co-CEO Mark Gerhard claimed the studio was a victim of corporate espionage and "saboteurs." The company will now pursue litigation against the people it accused in a bid to gather the money and pay off the debts. Gerhard had pinned the blame on a YouTube and TikTok management agency called Ritual Network, accusing it of tarnishing BARB’s reputation in a coordinated propaganda campaign. Ritual Network has denied all allegations that it orchestrated a $1 million smear campaign against MindsEye.

The proposal claims BARB’s investigations against “a number of third parties” are “the largest asset of the administration,” so it seems like all hopes at the company of paying off the debt are tied to litigation being successful.

Here is BARB's claim from the company document filed today:

Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating the circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment. The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties.

The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.

In May, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, issued what sounded like a nod to BARB’s struggles. "Making hits seems to get harder and harder and harder as entertainment industries mature," Zelnick said, speaking at the TD Cowen 54th Annual Technology, Media & Telecom Conference.

"The folks at Rockstar seem to be able to make these massive hits, and lots of other people have tried. Lots and lots, including former Rockstar employees. And so far, they haven't been able to do it."

items.title: GTA 6 Will Never Get a 60fps Update on PlayStation Pro as It's 'Not Powerful Enough'
items.description: There's bad news for any GTA 6 fans still hoping for a 60fps option on PlayStation 5 Pro.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
There's bad news for any GTA 6 fans still hoping for a 60fps option on PlayStation 5 Pro.

While Sony's beefier PS5 is arguably the most powerful console on the market today, even it is unable to run Rockstar's new masterpiece at 60fps. That's according to the game's technology production director Marc Chambers, who admitted that the PS5 Pro could only do so much.

Somewhat controversially, GTA 6 targets 30fps across all of its supported console platforms, with the same rate on everything from the under-powered Xbox Series S all the way up to PS5 Pro.

Naturally, there are other differences — and the game's PS5 Pro version has a few extra bells and whistles. But anyone expecting a better frame rate will need to temper their expectations — at least, perhaps, until the game's PC version arrives.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," Chambers told Kotaku.

That said, PS5 Pro still offers other improvements, he continued. "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination," Chambers noted. "On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity."

Speaking to IGN, Rockstar's co-studio head and head of development Rob Nelson said that "too much" of GTA 6 would have to fundamentally change for the game to target 60fps. "Too much, too much," he said in our big GTA 6 interview that went live today. "It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they're, like, 'Have you seen it?' There’s too many compromises that would've had to have been made to do that, is the short answer."

Today also brings more detail on how GTA 6 fares while running on Xbox Series S, where it is one of the first games to use AMD's FSR 4.1 on Xbox to upscale the graphically demanding game from 720p to 1080p.

items.title: GTA 6 Uses FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S to Upscale From 720p to 1080p
items.description: GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off.

Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, according to an interview with Wccftech. That would make GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox, and it's probably what made the game possible on the budget console.

I've already spent a bit of time with the Xbox Series S version of GTA 6, and while it does look a bit rough around the edges (literally), it looks better than I was expecting. Objects in the game are still incredibly detailed, but the edges of some objects – particularly distant buildings and hair – have a noticeable sheen of aliasing around them. But that lower resolution rendering is what lets the game mostly sit at around 30fps (though I did notice a couple drops down to the mid-20s.)

According to the interview, the Xbox Series S is the only version of the game that's running on FSR 4. Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game are instead using Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro is using PSSR 2.0. It shouldn't be surprising either, that the Xbox Series S is also running at the lowest input resolution out of all of the consoles at 720p, compared to 1440p on all of the other consoles.

When Wccftech asked Rockstar about the reasons it picked each upscaling solution, it said: "Part of that process [of targeting 30fps] was determining our base resolution and upscaling solution. We evaluated a variety of approaches for each console, then selected a combination of each that gave us the look and performance we needed." And, well, despite some noisy surfaces and aliasing, FSR 4 absolutely let Rockstar hit that 30fps target on the Xbox Series S.

Either way, GTA 6 is clearly a massive success. It's already the best-reviewed game of all time on Metacritic, and here at IGN we gave it a 10, with reviewer Luke Reilly saying: "exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

We're also live blogging GTA 6's launch, in what is surely going to be the biggest release in gaming history.

items.title: GTA 6 Is Now the Joint-Highest Rated Game of All Time
items.description: GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews in the past hour.

Rockstar's masterpiece currently sits with an all-time best score of 99 on Metacritic, an honor shared only with Nintendo's original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time release back in 1997 on N64, almost 30 years ago. No other game since has managed such a feat. (The new version of Ocarina for Switch 2 managed a paltry score of just 96.)

While both the N64 version of Ocarina and GTA 6 share a 99 average, GTA 6 has impressively managed to pull this off with more than six times' the number of reviews — over 120 at the time of writing, with over 100 of those listed with a perfect score. And while it's possible GTA 6's ranking could still slip down a point as more reviews are published, it would still be the best-rated game in nearly three decades.

Few others titles released in the recent memory have come anywhere close to this — though if you head back to the last console generation, Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Super Mario Odyssey both managed a 97 average, a standing they share with Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2.

items.title: KFC Australia Is Holding a Fake Funeral for Ann Alibi So You Can Take the Day Off for GTA 6
items.description: When famous people die, they break attendance records for funerals all the time. I have a feeling the upcoming funeral for the definitely real Ann Alibi might blow those attendance numbers out of the water though.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
When famous people die, they break attendance records for funerals all the time. I have a feeling the upcoming funeral for the definitely real Ann Alibi might blow those attendance numbers out of the water though.

KFC Australia is hosting a fake funeral so players can book work off for GTA 6. Or you could actually attend the funeral and get some free chicken — it depends what your priorities are.

“Ann Alibi was always there for us. Now you can be there for her,” the company said in an Instagram post.

“Join us Thursday 19 November for a funeral at KFC ROBINA, QLD, streamed live on Instagram from 11am AEDT. Any resemblance to a certain launch date is purely coincidental.”

The post is currently at 5.5k likes, but if it reaches 6k the company will offer free delivery throughout Australia for GTA 6 launch day. If you can’t get to Australia for a fake funeral and some free chicken, KFC plans to livestream the event. The service includes "a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest."

According to statistics, GTA 6 has already caused a 17% spike in time off requests at work this week as hype hits fever pitch for the game’s long-awaited launch.

Some companies have already got ahead of things. Palworld developer Pocketpair has given employees five days off to work their way through GTA 6’s open-world Florida.

If you want to keep up with all the news, follow along with our GTA 6 live blog, where we’ll be dropping all the news, collating all the buzz, and keeping everyone in that last-day-of-school vibe.

items.title: 'GTA Flu' Trends Online as Reports Suggest Thousands Will Skip School and Call in Sick at Work, With a Measurable Hit to Country's Economies
items.description: As GTA 6 launches around the world, businesses are bracing for a wave of so-called "GTA flu" as staff call in sick to play Rockstar's hugely-anticipated video game.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
As GTA 6 launches around the world, businesses are bracing for a wave of so-called "GTA flu" as staff call in sick to play Rockstar's hugely-anticipated video game.

The U.K.'s National Health Service has even issued guidance on how to stay healthy over the coming days and weeks, as millions begin long gaming sessions to explore Vice City. "Planning on dedicating time to gaming later this week?" reads a post by the NHS on Instagram.

"Try and take regular breaks, obviously. And be mindful of RSI (repetitive strain injury). That’s a term for pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers. Search online for 'NHS RSI' to get some advice on how to avoid getting any injuries."

Whether you're risking calling in sick to work or taking an unplanned day off from school, concern over the impact of GTA flu is spreading, particularly among teachers and parents. A school in Norwich, England has issued a warning about pupils declaring they have "GTA flu", Norfolk's Evening News reports, following a spate of similar messages to parents set out by schools across the U.K. and Ireland earlier this week. One school is even offering gift cards as an incentive for students to actually show up.

In Australia, requests for annual leave have reportedly jumped 29% around launch day compared to the same time period last year, News24 noted, with men aged 18 to 44 making up 75% of those vacation requests. According to The Sydney Morning Herald, meanwhile, GTA 6's launch is expected to cost the Australian enconomy at least $70 million, as it's expected that at least 1 in every 100 workers will call in sick.

U.K. tabloid The Daily Star claimed that "massive workplace carnage" would take place on both sides of the Atlantic, with 1.5 million US staff and 2.1 million U.K. employees expected to be absent, albeit via booking the day off. This could, the paper reported, drain U.S. national output "by 2% per cent in a single day, costing the American economy a staggering $1 billion in lost productivity."

While the flurry of excitement around GTA 6 may seem extreme to some, others would argue that this is a moment in gaming like no other — the launch of a fresh entry in an industry-defining franchise for the first time in over a decade, and after multiple high-profile delays. Indeed, even Strauss Zelnick, head of GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive, previously said he expected "a whole lot of people calling in sick on November 19."

items.title: How GTA 6 Came Together at Rockstar North
items.description: Current Rockstar North Co-Studio Head and Head of Development Rob Nelson seems relaxed for a man in Rockstar North’s bridge, essentially moments from steering what may well be the most anticipated entertainment product launch of all time into port — after 13 long years, no less.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Current Rockstar North Co-Studio Head and Head of Development Rob Nelson seems relaxed for a man in Rockstar North’s bridge, essentially moments from steering what may well be the most anticipated entertainment product launch of all time into port — after 13 long years, no less.

What’s perhaps more interesting, however, is how even Nelson is quite happy to concede that not even he quite knows how a game as fundamentally huge and absolutely astonishing as GTA 6 has come together so magically. Money and talent is only a part of the answer; the rest is perhaps a little more nebulous.

“I think it takes a lot of obstinance, really,” explains Nelson. “Just a sort of stubborn persistence in pursuit of the same thing for a long time, and a team that’s been together for a really long time. Now a really, really long time.

“And the answer is I don’t know. I mean, I only know my part of it, which is a part of it. And the stuff that [co-studio head] Aaron [Garbutt] does, and the stuff that [director of technology] Phil [Hooker] does, and the stuff that the programming team does, I don’t know. They just do it and we sort of build it up in layers.”

Nelson explains that Hooker sent an update through to the team very recently that showcased the progress of missions, areas, and features in the game over the last few years, and says it was “shocking to see how far it’s come.”

“Well, unfortunately, lots of people saw it in the hack that we had a few years ago — where [the game] was,” he says. “And I think in development you forget that. You forget the doldrums that you go through and you just sort of cling on to little wins every day, day by day or week by week. Sometimes they feel few and far between — certainly when you’re a few years out. And it’s just trust in the people that you’ve worked with for a long time that they’re going to hold up their end of it.”

“And this game had to rely on that. It probably sounds like a cliché answer, but this team and this game needed that more than we’ve ever had, because we’re larger than we’ve ever been — double the size that we were on RDR 2 — more spread out than we’ve ever been in terms of studios all over the world. Time zones. COVID.

“And you sit in it for week after week and just go, ‘Is this thing ever going to come together? Are we ever going to find it?’ But I think because we’ve been pursuing the same thing for a long time, every team knows what they generally want to do and want to evolve, and they just get on with it. And we work in these sort of eight-week sprints and pull a bunch of stuff together, evaluate it, make a bunch of notes, go back, iterate, iterate, iterate.”

Teams getting on with it appears to be precisely how fantastic and unexpected flourishes make their way to the final product. I note an example, which is the fact that there's now a unique animation solution for characters to get out of cars in skinny gaps, when the door can’t open all the way. Nelson lights up.

“There’s so many examples of it across the game, but that is a great example of one where the team just does their thing,” he says. “That hit a build one day and I played it just like you played it. And I was, like, ‘Holy shit, look at this. It’s amazing.’ I never asked for it. As far as I know, none of the other heads of development asked for it. The team did it. The animation directors decided that they wanted to do it.

“And that’s the most exciting thing, I think, for this team working on this stuff. It’s that there’s so many talented and experienced people working on it, and caring equally about their part, that every build is exciting. That’s I think what sustains you. It’s like every time you get a new build and there’s new stuff hitting it. It gives you energy to keep going.

“And it can be anything. It could be new ads on the radio, or just the radio going live for the first time. It can be new UI elements coming in to try, or little touches like that and you go, ‘Okay, all right, we’re just going to keep going.’ But, yeah, that’s a great example of something that just the team did off their own back.”

Nelson concedes that this approach does have to be managed, because without any guardrails, “every team will go crazy and go on forever.”

“And so there’s a bit of a contract there between all of us, including ourselves; having checks and balances in terms of where we push, how far we push, how hard we push, and how much resource [something] is worth, because everything is time and resource spent,” he says. “And contrary to what people think, we don’t have infinite money or time, or resource. So we do have to make decisions.”

On the topic of decisions, Rockstar’s confirmation that GTA 6 runs at 30 frames per second across all platforms including PS5 Pro became a popular talking point last week. Speaking with Nelson about what would have to fundamentally change about GTA 6 – and when – if the game had targeted 60fps, the Rockstar North veteran has a very simple answer.

“Too much, too much,” he says “It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer.”

In simple terms, the frame rate had to be limited somewhere in order to achieve Rockstar’s artistic vision. While the team is not ruling out things being different on future hardware, GTA 6’s sheer amount of visual fidelity, the complexity of its simulation, and the amount of systems and gameplay options it has would simply not be possible on current hardware at higher frame rate.

After playing it for the last three weeks I can’t imagine removing anything. Interestingly, it appears Nelson plays GTA 6 in an extremely similar way to the style of play I settled into during the review period – particularly in the way he prepares prior to open-world store and bank heists.

“I love just going into a store and buying a six-pack and walking down the street, drinking them one at a time, getting progressively more belligerent ’til I’m throwing the last two and talking to people,” grins Nelson. “And then I’ll call Lucia and see if she wants to hang out and sort of walk around”

“Just watching the world, the city, pass from day to night and seeing the population change and seeing people out for a night out. I think it’s that. I think it’s the fact that you can really feel like you’re embodying your version of these characters in that world. And then you could go from playing that solo to being on a date and walking around holding hands, and you can stroll down the beach or go into a nightclub and dance together, or go robbing together.”

As I discovered myself over the last few weeks, Nelson explains that the amount of preparation you want to do typically determines how successful your crime spree will be.

“I like to get just all of it ready,” he says. “I’ll just get a big vehicle, a big truck that I’ve souped up that can hold six bags, and I’ll park it somewhere close by. Then I’ll go steal a motorcycle that I don’t own and park it really close to where I’m going to go rob, go in and rob it, come out, take off on the motorcycle, stash the bags in the truck, go hit some more, [and] load the truck up with bags. Then you could either send your partner to go fence it, or go fence them yourself.”

And we work in these sort of eight-week sprints and pull a bunch of stuff together, evaluate it, make a bunch of notes, go back, iterate, iterate, iterate.”

Teams getting on with it appears to be precisely how fantastic and unexpected flourishes make their way to the final product. I note an example, which is the fact that there's now a unique animation solution for characters to get out of cars in skinny gaps, when the door can’t open all the way. Nelson lights up.

“There’s so many examples of it across the game, but that is a great example of one where the team just does their thing,” he says. “That hit a build one day and I played it just like you played it. And I was, like, ‘Holy shit, look at this. It’s amazing.’ I never asked for it. As far as I know, none of the other heads of development asked for it. The team did it. The animation directors decided that they wanted to do it.

“And that’s the most exciting thing, I think, for this team working on this stuff. It’s that there’s so many talented and experienced people working on it, and caring equally about their part, that every build is exciting. That’s I think what sustains you. It’s like every time you get a new build and there’s new stuff hitting it. It gives you energy to keep going.

“And it can be anything. It could be new ads on the radio, or just the radio going live for the first time. It can be new UI elements coming in to try, or little touches like that and you go, ‘Okay, all right, we’re just going to keep going.’ But, yeah, that’s a great example of something that just the team did off their own back.”

Nelson concedes that this approach does have to be managed, because without any guardrails, “every team will go crazy and go on forever.”

“And so there’s a bit of a contract there between all of us, including ourselves; having checks and balances in terms of where we push, how far we push, how hard we push, and how much resource [something] is worth, because everything is time and resource spent,” he says. “And contrary to what people think, we don’t have infinite money or time, or resource. So we do have to make decisions.”

On the topic of decisions, Rockstar’s confirmation that GTA 6 runs at 30 frames per second across all platforms including PS5 Pro became a popular talking point last week. Speaking with Nelson about what would have to fundamentally change about GTA 6 – and when – if the game had targeted 60fps, the Rockstar North veteran has a very simple answer.

“Too much, too much,” he says “It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer.”

In simple terms, the frame rate had to be limited somewhere in order to achieve Rockstar’s artistic vision. While the team is not ruling out things being different on future hardware, GTA 6’s sheer amount of visual fidelity, the complexity of its simulation, and the amount of systems and gameplay options it has would simply not be possible on current hardware at higher frame rate.

After playing it for the last three weeks I can’t imagine removing anything. Interestingly, it appears Nelson plays GTA 6 in an extremely similar way to the style of play I settled into during the review period – particularly in the way he prepares prior to open-world store and bank heists.

“I love just going into a store and buying a six-pack and walking down the street, drinking them one at a time, getting progressively more belligerent ’til I’m throwing the last two and talking to people,” grins Nelson. “And then I’ll call Lucia and see if she wants to hang out and sort of walk around”

“Just watching the world, the city, pass from day to night and seeing the population change and seeing people out for a night out. I think it’s that. I think it’s the fact that you can really feel like you’re embodying your version of these characters in that world. And then you could go from playing that solo to being on a date and walking around holding hands, and you can stroll down the beach or go into a nightclub and dance together, or go robbing together.”

As I discovered myself over the last few weeks, Nelson explains that the amount of preparation you want to do typically determines how successful your crime spree will be.

“I like to get just all of it ready,” he says. “I’ll just get a big vehicle, a big truck that I’ve souped up that can hold six bags, and I’ll park it somewhere close by. Then I’ll go steal a motorcycle that I don’t own and park it really close to where I’m going to go rob, go in and rob it, come out, take off on the motorcycle, stash the bags in the truck, go hit some more, [and] load the truck up with bags. Then you could either send your partner to go fence it, or go fence them yourself.”

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Story Missions — Here’s Why
items.description: Unlike previous games in the series, you can't replay missions in GTA 6.
items.author: Matt Purslow
items.content:
Think you’ll want to replay some of GTA 6’s most exciting missions? Well, you won’t be able to simply do that from any of its menus.

Now, not every game allows you to do this, so Rockstar’s latest is by no means an outlier in this regard, but seeing as practically every one of the studio’s games since The Ballad of Gay Tony expansion for GTA 4 has allowed you to do so, it is a little surprising.

GTA 6 is a little different from other games in the series, though. Its story flows and branches in small and big ways in a fluid manner not quite seen in any of the developer’s other open worlds. I’ve only completed one full playthrough myself, but can confirm that whole missions can play out differently based on decisions you didn’t even necessarily know you were making hours earlier. For example, one of GTA 6’s best missions, a daring high-stakes heist, can go relatively smoothly or turn out to be a much messier operation.

What’s most exciting is that, now knowing this, I’m left wondering how many new things I’ll see in the second playthrough I’ve just started, as much as I am looking forward to replaying the missions I can’t easily access. The decision by Rockstar not to include the option to revisit them at launch may well prove controversial, and who knows if it will be added post-launch, but I can see the argument as to why they’ve decided to do it this way.

With so many moving cogs and gears working away in the background to direct Jason and Lucia’s story down certain paths, both within main missions and seemingly random events in the open world, going back to change how certain things played out may prove problematic for its flow. With no medal system implemented — another Rockstar staple that grades your performance on a scale of bronze, silver, and gold — you’d want to replay these missions purely for the fun of it rather than chase high scores or personal best times.

There is one more traditional way around this problem to an extent, though, if you really do feel the urge to revisit moments: save files. GTA 6 gives you room for 15 manual save slots, and I’d highly recommend making a new one every 7% or so through the story so you’re never a million miles from reaching a point you may want to return to. With a main story that can take anywhere from 50 to 100 hours to complete depending on your playstyle, it’s always handy to have the opportunity to return to specific chapters.

We’ve got plenty more GTA 6 for you here at IGN. You can check out our review, or head over to our launch live blog, where I’ll be doing my best to answer as many of your spoiler-free questions as you may have about the game.
